analysis.label: Experimental SAR-Derived Flood Candidates — Unvalidated

areas.denominator: Valid analysis area = observed annual support plus separately reported inferred monthly non-water eligibility, on complete common-SAR neighborhoods. Candidates exclude observed annual permanent water. Unknown/unobserved reference pixels remain excluded; inferred support is not verified event-date land.

waterReference.inference: Only unknown annual pixels with >=3 observed monthly class-1 detections and zero observed monthly class-2 detections gain inferred eligibility. This is historical non-water evidence, not proof of event-date dry land or absence of permanent water.
waterReference.processingCaveat: No post-cutoff image entries are used. JRC v1.4 is a retrospective processed archive, not a product claimed to have been available contemporaneously in 2017.
waterReference.seasonalWater: Annual class 2 remains separately identified and potentially eligible; seasonal refilling can be a false candidate.

analysis.supportWarning: Experimental results cover 502.894 km² of 545.695 km² raster AOI. 0.000 km² has unknown historical-water support. 494.646 km² is inferred eligibility from historical monthly non-water detections, not verified event-date land. Do not interpret this as AOI-wide flood extent.

layer.label: Experimental SAR-Derived Flood Candidates — Unvalidated
layer.mask: Candidate pixels only; transparent remainder is not classified dry.

methodology.waterAttribution: Source: EC JRC/Google; Pekel et al., Nature 540, 418–422 (2016), doi:10.1038/nature20584
methodology.summary: VV dB → 10^(dB/10) → 30 m radius circular mean → 10*log10(mean power). Require later < -15 dB AND later-before < -3 dB AND before >= -15 dB; common complete neighborhoods; prior-year waterClass 3 excluded. No slope filter. Only unknown annual pixels with >=3 observed monthly class-1 detections and zero observed monthly class-2 detections gain inferred eligibility. This is historical non-water evidence, not proof of event-date dry land or absence of permanent water.
methodology.thresholdRationale: -3 dB is approximately a halving of radar power; -15 dB is an exploratory dark-surface screen. The conjunction screens newly darkened surfaces, not all negative changes. Neither threshold is empirically calibrated for Lower Kelani.

limitations: This mask identifies an exploratory threshold response, not confirmed flood extent, depth, peak inundation or detection accuracy.
The -15 dB and -3 dB thresholds are explicit exploratory defaults, not locally calibrated or transferred validation from another polarization or event.
S1A/S1B calibration, subpixel co-registration, baseline wetness and later historical water conditions remain unverified. In the 2017 research example, May 30 follows the documented event peak.
Urban double-bounce, vegetation, rough water, wet soil, speckle and radar shadow can cause omissions and false candidates. No slope, connectivity or terrain-shadow filter is applied.
Prior-year JRC water classes are 30 m Landsat-derived observations resampled by nearest neighbor; permanent-water omission and seasonal water remain possible. Unknown reference pixels are excluded.

A 30 m radius mean in linear power reduces speckle but blurs boundaries. The 10 m analysis grid does not establish independent 10 m mapping accuracy. Missing pixels are unobserved, never classified dry.

Optional monthly support is inferred eligibility from observed historical non-water months, not verified event-date land or confirmed absence of permanent water. Expanded support or candidate area does not imply better flood accuracy.

Annual classifications retain priority. Seasonal class 2 remains eligible and can produce seasonal-refilling false positives; zero water detections in the fallback window is not proof that water never occurred.
